findings.title: Redis OSS 2.8.24 replication group is past end of life
findings.description:
RedisReplicationGroup (AWS::ElastiCache::ReplicationGroup) in ElastiCache/Elasticache-snapshot.yaml declares Engine redis, EngineVersion 2.8.24 (line 147). Status EOL (source: AWS documentation, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/engine-versions.html): past end of life since 2023-01-13, not in the AWS Extended Support schedule, no fixes or security patches. AWS recommends 6.2 or higher. The documentation does not state whether a direct cross-engine upgrade from 2.8 to Valkey is allowed; confirm the path with `aws elasticache describe-cache-engine-versions` (or AWS Support) before planning a single-step upgrade. Because the version is older than 5.0.6, expect a 30-60 second write pause during failover. Risk Medium (score 3: +2 version older than 5.0.6, +1 no test or staging environment found). Topology: NumCacheClusters 2 with AutomaticFailoverEnabled true, so no single-node points. Recommendation (rule 3): Valkey 9 (9.1; confirm the newest 9.x in the target Region with DescribeCacheEngineVersions) - no Redis client libraries or application signals block it. Alternatives: Valkey 8 (8.2), Valkey 7.2 (in-place rollback to Redis OSS 7.1), Redis OSS 7.1 (no TLS requirement, no Valkey discount). Redis OSS 6.x is not recommended. Blocker: TransitEncryptionEnabled is not set (see blocker finding). The same stack is also defined in ElastiCache/Elasticache-snapshot.json; keep both templates in sync. No Extended Support cost is estimated because EOL versions are not in the Extended Support schedule. Live data not checked (live_access=off).

findings.title: In-transit encryption is not set for a Valkey target
findings.description: RedisReplicationGroup has no TransitEncryptionEnabled property (unset = off). The CloudFormation docs require TransitEncryptionEnabled when creating a Valkey replication group and cfn-lint rejects a Valkey replication group without it. Turning on TLS changes how every client connects, so it is not a safe silent edit; whether an in-place engine change also requires it is not confirmed. Proposed manual change: decide to enable TLS (TransitEncryptionMode: preferred first, then required) and move clients to TLS, or choose Redis OSS 7.1 (target C).

findings.title: Custom parameter group on family redis2.8
findings.description: AWS::ElastiCache::ParameterGroup RedisParameterGroup uses CacheParameterGroupFamily redis2.8 and sets no custom parameters (no non-default static values to carry over). The family must change with the engine (valkey9/valkey8/valkey7/redis7). Monitoring or runbooks that reference this group name must be updated after the change.

findings.title: Subnet group (no engine version)
findings.description: AWS::ElastiCache::SubnetGroup RedisSubnetGroup has no engine or version. Not affected by end of support; no change expected.

findings.title: Previous-generation node type cache.m3.medium
findings.description: RedisNodeType parameter allows only cache.m3.medium (previous generation). Whether this node type is offered for the chosen target engine and version is not stated in the references used; confirm with `aws elasticache describe-reserved-cache-nodes-offerings` / the supported node types page before the upgrade. Not counted as a blocker.
